rows: Risk or age group
Vaccine received previously
Options for vaccination
Adults aged ≥50 years
None or PCV7 only at any age

A single dose of PCV21, PCV20, or PCV15. If PCV15 is administered, a single dose of PPSV23* should be administered ≥1 year after the PCV15 dose. A minimum interval of 8 weeks can be considered if PCV15 is used in adults with an immunocompromising condition,† cochlear implant, or CSF leak.
PPSV23 only
A single dose of PCV21, PCV20, or PCV15 ≥1 year after the last PPSV23 dose.
PCV13 only
A single dose of PCV21 or PCV20 ≥1 year after the PCV13 dose.
PCV13 at any age and PPSV23 at age <65 years
A single dose of PCV21 or PCV20 ≥5 years after the last pneumococcal vaccine dose.
PCV13 at any age and PPSV23 at age ≥65 years

Shared clinical decision-making is recommended regarding administration of either a single dose of PCV21 or PCV20 for any adult aged ≥65 years who has completed the recommended vaccination series with both PCV13 and PPSV23 (i.e., PPSV23 administered at age ≥65 years) but PCV21, PCV20, or PCV15 not yet received. If a decision to administer PCV21 or PCV20 is made, a single dose is recommended ≥5 years after the last pneumococcal vaccine dose.
Adults aged 19–49 years with an immunocompromising condition,† a CSF leak, or a cochlear implant
None or PCV7 only at any age
A single dose of PCV21, PCV20, or PCV15. If PCV15 is used, administer a single dose of PPSV23* ≥8 weeks after the PCV15 dose.
PPSV23 only
A single dose of PCV21, PCV20, or PCV15 ≥1 year after the last PPSV23 dose.
PCV13 only
A single dose of PCV21 or PCV20 administered ≥1 year after the PCV13 dose.
PCV13 and 1 dose of PPSV23

A single dose of PCV21 or PCV20 ≥5 years after the last pneumococcal vaccine dose. The pneumococcal vaccination series is complete, and it need not be followed by additional pneumococcal vaccine doses.
PCV13 and 2 doses of PPSV23

The pneumococcal vaccination recommendations should be reviewed again when the person turns age 50 years. Alternatively, a single dose of either PCV21 or PCV20 should be administered ≥5 years after the last pneumococcal vaccine dose. notes: MMWR article reprint PDF exactly as served (8 pages, US Letter, two columns). Page 1: issue masthead ('U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention', 'MMWR' logo, 'Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report', 'Weekly / Vol. 74 / No. 1', 'January 9, 2025'), title, authors, Abstract and Introduction in two columns, footnote *, an 'INSIDE' box listing other articles of the issue, a Continuing Education box and the HHS/CDC logo block. Pages 2-6: body, FIGURE (page 2), editorial-board box (page 2), Summary box (page 4), TABLE (page 5), BOX (page 6), acknowledgments, work group, author affiliations and disclosures. Pages 7-8: References 1-33. Headings: the first line of the title (the title is 3 lines; the listed string is the part on line 1), the blue centred section headings (Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Rationale and Evidence, Recommendations for Use of PCV, Acknowledgments, ACIP Pneumococcal Vaccines Work Group, References) and the bold run-over subsection headings; 'Pneumococcal Disease Incidence in Adults Aged' is the printed heading without its final '≥19 Years' (the ≥ sign's code point cannot be seen). The 'Summary' box labels, the FIGURE/TABLE/BOX captions and the 'INSIDE' items are not headings. ordered: 8 body-text anchors on pages 1 (left, right), 2, 3, 4 (left, right), 5 and 6; none from a footnote, box, figure, table or reference, so footnote placement does not change order_score. must_contain: 29 phrases, each printed once, none crossing a column or page break or a hyphenated line end; 4 are footnotes or table notes (footnote *, footnote **, footnote §§, TABLE footnote *), 1 is from the Summary box, 2 from the BOX, 1 from References. TABLE: complete. The first column labels a row group and is printed once, on the group's first row; the other rows of the group have an empty first cell (empty expected cells are not scored, so repeating the label costs precision only). Cells are written as printed, wrapped lines joined with a space; footnote markers are kept ('PPSV23*' normalizes to 'ppsv23'; '†' and '§' stay). Most cells contain '≥', and two labels contain an en dash ('19–49'); these are written as the visible characters U+2265 and U+2013, an assumption the blind protocol could not verify against the text layer. The FIGURE (page 2) is a grid of coloured cells whose meaning is in the colour, so it is not a table check. Noise (visible furniture): the running header 'Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report' tops pages 2-8 and the same words are the page-1 masthead, so a faithful conversion has at most 1; the footer 'U.S. Department of Health and Human Services | Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | MMWR | January 9, 2025 | Vol. 74 | No. 1' is on pages 2-8 (7 times; page 1 has the logo block instead), checked through its last segment, max 1 (the '|' separators normalize to spaces; 'U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' is not used because the page-2 editorial box also prints it). Absent: split forms of eight one-word line-end hyphenations in body text (page 1 'conju-/gate', 'trans-/mission'; page 3 'unpub-/lished', 'annu-/ally', 'recommenda-/tion'; page 4 'diag-/nostic', 'assump-/tions', 'experi-/encing'); compounds broken at a line end ('PCV-/naïve', 'non-/Black', 'non-/Hispanic', 'double-/blind', 'placebo-/controlled', 'toxoid–/containing') are not listed. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 150-300 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, cover art, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants, the '>=' sign), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
